1. Identification Strategy
I will use an instrumental variables (IV) strategy embedded in a two-way fixed effects panel design. The core idea is to isolate the exogenous component of a borrower’s prior loan spread that was driven by aggregate credit-market tightness at the time of the firm’s last borrowing, and test whether that exogenous “anchor” persists in the pricing of the new loan even after controlling for current borrower fundamentals and current market conditions.

Concretely:
- Endogenous regressor: the borrower’s last-loan all-in-drawn spread (AISD_last), which reflects both borrower-specific risk at the time and the aggregate state then.
- Instrument: market-wide credit tightness at the time of the firm’s last borrowing (e.g., the leave-one-out average AISD in Dealscan or external high-yield OAS/Baa-Aaa spread), measured at the quarter of the last loan. This moves AISD_last for reasons orthogonal to firm-specific risk.
- Outcome: the current loan’s AISD (AISD_current).
- Fixed effects: firm fixed effects to absorb time-invariant heterogeneity, and current calendar time fixed effects (year-quarter) to absorb the entire current macro state.
- Controls: rich set of current loan terms, current borrower financials (Compustat), current S&P rating category (including unrated), relationship controls, and time since last loan; plus lagged borrower controls at the time of the last loan to further purge selection on timing.

This is effectively a “timing-IV” or shift-share IV design: exposure to tight (loose) credit when the firm last borrowed is plausibly quasi-random after conditioning, and it varies across firms arriving to the market in the same current quarter. I will also report a reduced-form version that regresses current AISD directly on last-period aggregate tightness with the same FE and controls. As complementary evidence, I will implement a binned difference-in-differences-style specification that compares firms whose prior borrowing occurred in top versus bottom quartiles of past market tightness.

2. Treatment and Control
- Treatment variable (continuous, preferred):
  - Z_i,t ≡ MarketSpread_last_i: an index of aggregate credit-market tightness in the quarter when firm i last borrowed prior to current loan t. Primary measure: leave-one-out average AISD across syndicated loans in Dealscan in that last-loan quarter (excluding firm i). Robust alternatives: Merrill/ICE US high-yield OAS; Moody’s Baa–Aaa spread; bank loan index spread if available.
  - Endogenous regressor: AISD_last_i (firm i’s actual observed last-loan AISD).
- Control group / counterfactual:
  - Cross-sectional counterfactual is firms borrowing in the same current calendar quarter with similar current fundamentals and loan features but whose last borrowing occurred under looser aggregate conditions (low Z_i,t).
- Binary treatment (for binned DID robustness):
  - Treated_i,t = 1 if MarketSpread_last_i is in the top quartile (or tercile) of its historical distribution; Control_i,t = 1 if in the bottom quartile. Middle group optional or excluded.
- Treatment timing / event date:
  - Event date is the current loan origination date. Treatment “assignment” was realized at the borrower’s last-loan date (the most recent loan strictly at least 1 year before the current loan).
- Running variable and cutoff (RDD):
  - Not applicable for the main design. As an optional complementary design, we can implement local RDs around sharp market shocks (e.g., Aug–Oct 1998 LTCM/Russia, Sept 2001, mid-2007), comparing firms whose last loans fell just before vs. just after shocks. This yields an additional validity check but is not the primary strategy.

3. Key Identifying Assumptions
- Relevance (IV): Aggregate market tightness at the last-loan quarter strongly predicts the borrower’s last-loan AISD.
  - Plausible: Marketwide spreads move all-in-drawn spreads materially. We will show strong first-stage F-statistics. Use multiple instruments for strength and robustness.
- Exclusion (IV): Conditional on firm FE, current time FE, current borrower/loan controls, and lagged borrower controls, last-period aggregate tightness affects today’s AISD only via the anchor it imprints through prior deal terms/relationship and not through other channels that persist to today.
  - Plausibility: Any macro effects from the past that operate through the borrower’s current balance sheet or risk should be captured by current financials and ratings; current macro is absorbed by current time FE. We will control for last-loan borrower characteristics and last-loan features to limit timing selection. We will probe heterogeneity by same vs. different lead arranger to explore mechanism (relationship anchoring vs. market memory).
- As-good-as-random timing of last borrowing conditional on observables and FE: After conditioning on firm FE, lagged borrower controls, and loan purpose, the variation in Z_i,t across firms borrowing today is not driven by unobserved persistent shocks that still affect pricing today.
  - Plausibility: Some concern remains that urgent funding needs during tight times select particular firms. We address this with rich lagged controls, time-since-last-loan fixed effects, loan-purpose fixed effects, and selection checks (IPW).
- Stable unit treatment value (no spillovers): A firm’s last-period market tightness exposure does not directly change other firms’ current pricing conditional on current time FE.
  - Plausible: Current time FE nets out contemporaneous spillovers; cross-firm past exposures don’t interact in a way that varies within current quarter.
- Correct specification/inference: Sufficient controls and two-way clustering for accurate standard errors.
  - Plausible with firm and time clustering.

4. Threats to Identification and Mitigations
- Endogenous last-loan timing due to persistent unobservables:
  - Threat: Firms that borrowed under tight conditions may have had adverse private shocks that persist beyond observed covariates, inflating current AISD.
  - Mitigations:
    - Firm fixed effects to remove time-invariant heterogeneity.
    - Rich lagged controls at last-loan time: leverage, ROA, size, rating, stock returns/volatility, current ratio, market-to-book, plus last-loan characteristics (collateral, covenants, maturity, performance pricing, purpose).
    - Time-since-last-loan fixed effects to equalize horizon since prior borrowing.
    - Placebo: include “two-loans-ago” market tightness; effect should be much smaller once last-loan exposure is included.
    - Event-window RD around major shocks as a validation exercise.
- Relationship-specific/bank private information confounding:
  - Threat: Same-lead arrangers may carry forward private info from last deal; last spread proxies for private risk rather than anchoring.
  - Mitigations:
    - Include lead-arranger FE and/or bank×current-time FE to absorb bank pricing policies.
    - Include same-lead indicator and interact with Z_i,t to test whether effects concentrate when the bank is the same (anchoring/relationship) versus when switching (market memory). Finding effects even when switching supports pricing anchor rather than private information.
    - Control for arranger market share and syndicate structure.
- Sample selection/attrition into repeat borrowing:
  - Threat: Only firms that return appear; those treated by tight last markets may be less likely to return unless in distress, biasing estimates.
  - Mitigations:
    - Inverse probability weighting: model return-to-market probability using the universe of Dealscan borrowers, with predictors measured at last loan, and weight the estimating sample.
    - Restrict to firms with exactly two loans (balanced two-loan panels) as a robustness check.
    - Show that treatment predicts return probability; report bounds (e.g., Oster or trimming).

5. R Code Outline
Note: This is executable pseudocode assuming CSVs exist. We use fixest for FE and IV.

# Packages
library(data.table)
library(lubridate)
library(fixest)
library(sandwich)

# 1) Load data
deals <- fread("dealscan_loans.csv")      # loan-level tranches; includes firm_id, loan_id, start_date, AISD, amount, maturity, collateral, covenants, perf_pricing, fees, lead_arranger_id, arranger_mktshare, purpose
comp  <- fread("compustat_quarterly.csv") # firm_id, fqtr_date, assets, sales, leverage, roa, curr_ratio, m2b, ret_q, ret_vol, sp_rating
mkt   <- fread("market_spreads_quarterly.csv") # yq, hy_oas, baa_aaa, ted, (optional) avg_AISD_all

# 2) Basic preprocessing
deals[, start_date := as.Date(start_date)]
deals[, yq_cur := paste0(year(start_date), "Q", quarter(start_date))]

setorder(deals, firm_id, start_date)
# Identify last loan for each current loan
deals[, last_loan_date := shift(start_date, 1L, type = "lag"), by = firm_id]
deals[, last_loan_id   := shift(loan_id,   1L, type = "lag"), by = firm_id]
deals[, AISD_last      := shift(AISD,      1L, type = "lag"), by = firm_id]
deals[, yq_last := ifelse(!is.na(last_loan_date), paste0(year(last_loan_date), "Q", quarter(last_loan_date)), NA)]

# Keep repeat borrowers with at least 1 year between loans
deals <- deals[!is.na(last_loan_date) & as.numeric(start_date - last_loan_date) >= 365]

# 3) Create market tightness measures at last-loan time
# Option A: Use external series
mkt[, yq := as.factor(yq)]
deals[, yq_last := as.factor(yq_last)]
deals <- merge(deals, mkt[, .(yq, hy_oas, baa_aaa)], by.x = "yq_last", by.y = "yq", all.x = TRUE, suffixes = c("", "_last"))
setnames(deals, c("hy_oas", "baa_aaa"), c("hy_oas_last", "baa_aaa_last"))

# Option B: Leave-one-out average Dealscan AISD in last quarter
avg_a <- deals[ , .(avg_AISD_q = mean(AISD, na.rm=TRUE)), by = yq_cur]
setnames(avg_a, "yq_cur", "yq")
deals <- merge(deals, avg_a, by.x = "yq_last", by.y = "yq", all.x = TRUE)
# Leave-one-out for last loan quarter (when the firm's own last loan contributed to the average)
# First, get the quarter average including all; then compute LOO by adjusting if last loan exists in data
# We need AISD at last loan_id and the quarter count
cnt_q <- deals[, .N, by = yq_last]
setnames(cnt_q, c("yq_last", "N"), c("yq", "N_q"))
deals <- merge(deals, cnt_q, by.x = "yq_last", by.y = "yq", all.x = TRUE)
# Retrieve the AISD at last loan_id via self-merge
last_info <- unique(deals[, .(firm_id, last_loan_id, AISD_last, yq_last)])
setnames(last_info, "last_loan_id", "loan_id")
last_info <- last_info[!is.na(loan_id)]
# Compute leave-one-out market spread for the last-loan quarter
deals[, mktspread_last_loo := ifelse(N_q > 1 & !is.na(AISD_last) & !is.na(avg_AISD_q),
                                     (avg_AISD_q * N_q - AISD_last)/(N_q - 1),
                                     avg_AISD_q)]

# 4) Merge borrower financials at current quarter (closest non-missing prior quarter)
comp[, fqtr_date := as.Date(fqtr_date)]
setorder(comp, firm_id, fqtr_date)
# Function to roll-join last observation carried forward up to loan date
setkey(comp, firm_id, fqtr_date)
setkey(deals, firm_id, start_date)
deals <- comp[deals, roll = Inf]  # adds latest comp row with fqtr_date <= start_date

# Also merge lagged borrower controls at last-loan date
# Create a Compustat yq and join on yq_last
comp[, yq := paste0(year(fqtr_date), "Q", quarter(fqtr_date))]
setkey(comp, firm_id, yq)
setkey(deals, firm_id, yq_last)
lag_vars <- c("assets","sales","leverage","roa","curr_ratio","m2b","ret_q","ret_vol","sp_rating")
comp_lag <- unique(comp[, c("firm_id","yq", lag_vars), with=FALSE])
setnames(comp_lag, lag_vars, paste0(lag_vars, "_last"))
deals <- merge(deals, comp_lag, by.x = c("firm_id","yq_last"), by.y = c("firm_id","yq"), all.x = TRUE)

# 5) Construct controls and FE identifiers
deals[, ln_amount := log(pmax(amount, 1))]
deals[, ln_maturity := log(pmax(maturity, 1))]
deals[, secured := as.integer(collateral == 1)]
deals[, perf_price := as.integer(perf_pricing == 1)]
deals[, yq_cur := as.factor(yq_cur)]
deals[, firm_id := as.factor(firm_id)]
deals[, arranger_id := as.factor(lead_arranger_id)]
deals[, same_lead := as.integer(lead_arranger_id == shift(lead_arranger_id, 1L, type = "lag")), by = firm_id]
# Time since last loan
deals[, months_since_last := as.integer((start_date - last_loan_date)/30)]
deals[, months_bin := cut(months_since_last, breaks=c(12,24,36,60,120,Inf), include.lowest=TRUE)]

# 6) Define instrument(s) and endogenous regressor
deals[, Z_last := mktspread_last_loo]           # primary instrument from Dealscan
deals[, Z_hy  := hy_oas_last]                   # robustness instrument
# Endogenous regressor:
deals[, AISD_last := AISD_last]

# 7) Main IV specification: current AISD on instrumented AISD_last
# Controls: current borrower and loan controls; FE: firm and current yq
iv_formula <- AISD ~ ln_amount + ln_maturity + secured + perf_price + fees + arranger_mktshare +
  assets + sales + leverage + roa + curr_ratio + m2b + ret_q + ret_vol +
  i(sp_rating, ref = "Unrated") + i(purpose) + i(months_bin) | 
  firm_id + yq_cur | 
  AISD_last ~ Z_last

est_iv <- feols(iv_formula, data = deals,
                vcov = ~ firm_id + yq_cur)  # two-way clustered SEs
summary(est_iv)

# 8) Reduced-form: current AISD directly on last-period market tightness
rf_formula <- AISD ~ Z_last + ln_amount + ln_maturity + secured + perf_price + fees + arranger_mktshare +
  assets + sales + leverage + roa + curr_ratio + m2b + ret_q + ret_vol +
  i(sp_rating, ref = "Unrated") + i(purpose) + i(months_bin) | 
  firm_id + yq_cur

est_rf <- feols(rf_formula, data = deals, vcov = ~ firm_id + yq_cur)
summary(est_rf)

# 9) Robustness check A: Alternative instrument (external HY OAS)
est_iv_hy <- feols(AISD ~ ln_amount + ln_maturity + secured + perf_price + fees + arranger_mktshare +
                     assets + sales + leverage + roa + curr_ratio + m2b + ret_q + ret_vol +
                     i(sp_rating, ref = "Unrated") + i(purpose) + i(months_bin) |
                     firm_id + yq_cur |
                     AISD_last ~ Z_hy,
                   data = deals, vcov = ~ firm_id + yq_cur)
summary(est_iv_hy)

# 10) Robustness check B: Heterogeneity by same vs different lead arranger
est_rf_het <- feols(AISD ~ Z_last * same_lead + ln_amount + ln_maturity + secured + perf_price + fees + arranger_mktshare +
                      assets + sales + leverage + roa + curr_ratio + m2b + ret_q + ret_vol +
                      i(sp_rating, ref = "Unrated") + i(purpose) + i(months_bin) |
                      firm_id + yq_cur,
                    data = deals, vcov = ~ firm_id + yq_cur)
summary(est_rf_het)

# 11) Optional: Binary treatment (top vs bottom quartile of Z_last)
q <- quantile(deals$Z_last, probs=c(0.25,0.75), na.rm=TRUE)
deals[, treat_high := as.integer(Z_last >= q[2])]
deals[, control_low := as.integer(Z_last <= q[1])]
est_bin <- feols(AISD ~ i(treat_high, ref = 0) + ln_amount + ln_maturity + secured + perf_price + fees + arranger_mktshare +
                   assets + sales + leverage + roa + curr_ratio + m2b + ret_q + ret_vol +
                   i(sp_rating, ref = "Unrated") + i(purpose) + i(months_bin) |
                   firm_id + yq_cur,
                 data = deals[control_low==1 | treat_high==1], vcov = ~ firm_id + yq_cur)
summary(est_bin)

6. Expected Results
- Direction: Positive. Firms whose last borrowing occurred when aggregate credit spreads were high should pay higher spreads today, even after conditioning on current fundamentals and current market conditions. Conversely, those last borrowing in loose markets should enjoy a discount.
- Magnitude (prior): For every 100 bps increase in aggregate market tightness at the last-loan date, I expect 10–30 bps higher AISD today (elasticity 0.1–0.3). The effect should decay with time since last loan and be stronger when the same lead arranger is retained (anchoring/relationship channel), but still present when switching (market memory).

7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (IV design)
- C1: Strong first stage (instrument relevance): 1
  - Market-wide tightness at last loan should strongly predict last-loan AISD; we will report first-stage F > 10 and use multiple instruments.
- C2: Exclusion restriction plausibility: 0.5
  - Main residual concern is persistent unobservables tied to last-loan timing. We mitigate with firm FE, rich current and lagged controls, and show placebo/two-loans-ago and RD robustness.
- C3: No omitted time-varying confounders after FE and controls: 0.5
  - Current time FE and current borrower controls help; remaining concern is differential recovery trajectories since the last loan. We add months-since-last-loan FE and lagged controls.
- C4: Stable sample/selection addressed: 0.5
  - We will assess and correct with IPW and balanced subsamples; some residual selection may remain.
- C5: Correct inference and functional form: 1
  - Two-way clustered SEs at firm and current time; alternative specifications (reduced-form, binary treatment, external instruments) for robustness.

Overall, the timing-IV with rich FE and controls leverages plausibly exogenous variation in past market tightness across firms arriving to borrow in the same current period, providing a credible test of whether prior borrowing costs causally anchor new-loan pricing beyond what current fundamentals and market conditions justify.
